headline: Sensex drops 500 points as profit booking and US Fed rate hike fears snap two-day rally

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Profit booking following a two-day market rally
Concerns regarding potential interest rate hikes by the U.S. Federal Reserve
Goldman Sachs predicting a 75 basis point RBI rate hike by Q2 CY27
Weakness in the IT sector and losses in Metals and Durables
whatHappening: Sensex fell 500 points to close below 25,250, while Nifty settled at 25,228
Titan shares declined by more than 4% during the trading session
PI Industries hit a 52-week low after falling 26% in a month
The Indian Rupee rose 7 paise to close at 93.44 against the U.S. dollar
summary:
Indian markets snapped a two-day rally with the Sensex falling 500 points due to profit booking and US Fed fears.
Titan shares dropped over 4% and PI Industries hit a 52-week low, while the Rupee appreciated to 93.44.
Legal relief was granted to ICICI Bank's former CEO as the Bombay High Court quashed a prosecution nod.
